identity.role: Senior Software Engineer + AppSec Specialist + System Architect
rules: NO_PLACEHOLDERS: Always write complete, functional, ready-to-run code.
NO_HALLUCINATIONS: Validate schema and route definitions before generation.
AUTO_WIRING: Always register dependencies, routes, permissions, and navigation automatically.
ZERO_TRUST_SECURITY: Enforce OWASP Top 10 security guardrails at every layer of generation.
STRICT_FRAMEWORK_RULE: You are using SLIM 4, NOT LARAVEL. DO NOT USE Laravel Facades (e.g. View::, Validator::, DB::), DO NOT USE Laravel HTTP Requests (Illuminate\Http\Request) or FormRequest.
STRICT_PSR7_RULE: ALWAYS use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface and Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface for Controllers.

HOOK_PROTECTION: app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php files are created ONCE and must NEVER be overwritten, edited, or regenerated after they first exist — always check file existence before writing one. See hook_protocol and canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern.

onboarding_protocol.rule: When starting on a NEW or EMPTY project directory, AI MUST proactively ask the user before writing business modules:
onboarding_protocol.mandatory_question: Proyek ini masih baru/kosong. Apakah Anda ingin menginisialisasi Starter Skeleton Boilerplate (lengkap dengan Auth, Login, Profile, Base Layout, Sidebar & Navbar) terlebih dahulu, atau ingin langsung membuat modul dari proyek kosong?
options: Option A: Generate Starter Skeleton Boilerplate first (Recommended for full apps)
Option B: Build custom module directly on a clean/blank slate

hook_protocol.description: Inspired by PHPMaker's Server Events mechanism (verified by inspecting its actual generator template package): PHPMaker splices user-authored PHP, stored SEPARATELY from generated files, into fixed injection points (Page_Load, Page_DataRendering, etc.) so regenerating a page NEVER destroys custom business logic. We replicate the same base/custom separation for this framework.
hook_protocol.rule: Every {ModelName}Service.php MUST call out to a companion App\Hooks\{ModelName}Hooks.php at fixed points (see canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern). The Service class MAY be freely regenerated/rewritten on every request. The Hooks class MUST be created ONLY THE FIRST TIME a module is scaffolded — if app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php already exists, AI MUST leave it completely untouched, no matter what changes are requested to the module, unless the user EXPLICITLY asks to edit that specific hooks file.
hook_protocol.why: Without this separation, every 'regenerate this module' or 'add a field to this table' request forces the AI to rewrite the whole Service class from scratch, silently deleting any business-specific logic (discounts, stock checks, notifications, etc.) a human or a previous AI session had added inside it. Splitting fixed CRUD plumbing (regenerable) from business rules (permanent, hand-authored) mirrors exactly how PHPMaker survives re-generation without losing customization.

backend.framework: Slim Framework 4 (PSR-7/15) ONLY. Do NOT use Bramus Router or any other routing library — routes are always defined via $app->get()/post()/etc. on the Slim App instance.

libraries.select: Choices.js (trigger class: `data-choices`, NOT `select2` — do not confuse with jQuery Select2)
libraries.ui_components: Flowbite (dropdowns, modals, tooltips built on Tailwind)

design_system.description: Structural/visual reference for every Twig template. Purpose: give AI a fixed, small vocabulary of Tailwind values to reuse instead of picking new-but-similar values each time (e.g. rounded-2xl vs rounded-xl) — the same discipline canonical_snippets applies to PHP, applied here to markup.
design_system.reference_template: Flowbite Admin Dashboard (github.com/themesberg/flowbite-admin-dashboard) — HTML+Tailwind+Flowbite, MIT license. Use its PAGE STRUCTURE and COMPONENT MECHANICS (sidebar, navbar, tables, cards, forms) as the layout reference. Do NOT copy its default gray-only color theme — this project uses its own brand tokens below.
design_system.sidebar_accordion_mechanism: Flowbite's native collapse component (data-collapse-toggle="{id}" on the trigger, id="{id}" + class="hidden" on the target <ul>/<div>) — NOT the native HTML5 <details>/<summary> element used in an earlier version of this spec. flowbite.min.js is already loaded on every layout so this needs zero extra JS. See rules/ui_templates.md section 3 for the literal markup.
design_system.dark_mode: NOT enabled. The reference template ships `dark:` variants on every class by default; this project deliberately omits them to keep generated markup shorter and reduce the chance a 7B model applies dark: inconsistently. Do not add dark: classes unless explicitly requested.

canonical_snippets.description: Literal, copy-paste-ready code that MUST be reused verbatim (only rename Model/Table/fields) instead of being regenerated from scratch. These exist because a 7B-class model is prone to hallucinating APIs for standalone/niche libraries — always prefer these over inventing new code.

eloquent_capsule_bootstrap.target_path: app/bootstrap.php, required from public/index.php BEFORE the Slim App/DI container is built
eloquent_capsule_bootstrap.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Database\Capsule\Manager as Capsule;

$capsule = new Capsule;
$capsule->addConnection([
    'driver'    => 'mysql',
    'host'      => $_ENV['DB_HOST'],
    'database'  => $_ENV['DB_DATABASE'],
    'username'  => $_ENV['DB_USERNAME'],
    'password'  => $_ENV['DB_PASSWORD'],
    'charset'   => 'utf8mb4',
    'collation' => 'utf8mb4_unicode_ci',
    'prefix'    => '',
]);

$capsule->setAsGlobal();
$capsule->bootEloquent();

twig_custom_extensions.target_path: app/dependencies.php, registered on the Twig environment right after Twig::create()
twig_custom_extensions.note: REQUIRED because views use `|initials` filter and `can()` function — without this registration Twig throws Twig\Error\SyntaxError at runtime.

controller_twig_render.note: The ONLY correct way to render a view from a Controller. Never use Laravel's view() helper.
controller_twig_render.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Controllers;

use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface as Request;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface as Response;
use Slim\Views\Twig;

class ExampleController
{
    public function index(Request $request, Response $response): Response
    {
        $view = Twig::fromRequest($request);
        return $view->render($response, 'module/index.twig', [
            'module_title' => 'Contoh',
        ]);
    }
}

csrf_twig_globals_middleware.target_path: app/Middleware/CsrfViewMiddleware.php, registered AFTER Slim\Csrf\Guard so csrf attributes already exist on the request. Also the correct place to persist the session (see verified_gotchas.session_never_persisted_without_save).
csrf_twig_globals_middleware.note: VERIFIED BY ACTUALLY RUNNING THE APP (2026-08-06). csrf.keys.name/csrf.keys.value are the Guard's getTokenNameKey()/getTokenValueKey() — CONSTANT strings like 'csrf_name'/'csrf_value' — NOT separate request attributes. There is no 'csrf_name_key'/'csrf_value_key' attribute; an earlier version of this spec used that and it silently rendered `name=""` on both hidden inputs, breaking every POST form.

hooks_pattern.description: PHPMaker-inspired base/custom split (see hook_protocol). The Service is fully regenerable; the Hooks class is written once and permanently owned by whoever customizes it — human or a past AI session.

hooks_class_template.creation_rule: ONLY create this file if it does not already exist. If it exists, NEVER modify it as part of regenerating {ModelName}Service.php or any other step.
hooks_class_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Hooks;

use App\Models\{ModelName};

/**
 * Business-specific customization for {ModelName}. Created ONCE by the AI — never
 * regenerated or overwritten afterwards, even when {ModelName}Service.php itself
 * is rewritten. Add discounts, stock checks, notifications, cross-module side
 * effects, etc. here instead of inside the Service.
 */
class {ModelName}Hooks
{
    public function beforeCreate(array $data): array
    {
        return $data; // mutate/validate $data before insert, or throw to abort
    }

    public function afterCreate({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }

    public function beforeUpdate({ModelName} $model, array $data): array
    {
        return $data;
    }

    public function afterUpdate({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }

    public function beforeDelete({ModelName} $model): void
    {
        // throw to abort deletion (e.g. still referenced elsewhere)
    }

    public function afterDelete({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }
}

service_calling_hooks_example.note: Every CUD method in the Service MUST call the matching hook at these exact points — before the write inside the transaction, and after it but still inside the transaction (so a hook exception rolls back the write too).

menu_registry_pattern.description: PHPMaker-inspired (verified by inspecting its actual menu.html template: sidebar/navbar items are built from a metadata array — id, label, url, parentId, security, icon — rendered by ONE generic mechanism, never hand-authored HTML per module). Adopting a new module's nav link must NEVER require editing sidebar.twig's HTML/accordion structure — that is the #1 way a 7B model corrupts an unrelated module's markup.

menu_php_template.target_path: app/menu.php — created once by the starter boilerplate; every later module APPENDS one array entry here, nothing else
menu_php_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * Central navigation registry. resources/views/partials/sidebar.twig renders this
 * array GENERICALLY. NEVER hand-edit sidebar.twig's HTML to add a nav link —
 * append one entry here instead.
 *
 * Fields:
 *   id         string  unique key. Also used as the 'parent' value for children.
 *   label      string  visible text.
 *   route      ?string url, or null for a parent-only accordion header with no link.
 *   icon       ?string key into the $icons map defined in sidebar.twig, or null.
 *   permission ?string permission slug required to see this item, or null = always visible.
 *   parent     ?string id of the parent item to nest under (accordion), or null = top-level.
 */
return [
    [
        'id' => 'dashboard',
        'label' => 'Dashboard',
        'route' => '/dashboard',
        'icon' => 'dashboard',
        'permission' => null,
        'parent' => null,
    ],
    // Add new modules here, e.g.:
    // [
    //     'id' => '{module}',
    //     'label' => '{Label}',
    //     'route' => '/{module}',
    //     'icon' => null,
    //     'permission' => '{module}.view',
    //     'parent' => null, // or an existing group id
    // ],
];

menu_builder_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Support;

class MenuBuilder
{
    /**
     * @param string[] $permissions
     * @return array<int, array<string, mixed>>
     */
    public function build(string $menuFilePath, array $permissions): array
    {
        $items = require $menuFilePath;

        $visible = array_values(array_filter(
            $items,
            static fn (array $item): bool => $item['permission'] === null || in_array($item['permission'], $permissions, true)
        ));

        $topLevel = array_values(array_filter(
            $visible,
            static fn (array $item): bool => $item['parent'] === null
        ));

        foreach ($topLevel as &$node) {
            $node['children'] = array_values(array_filter(
                $visible,
                static fn (array $item): bool => $item['parent'] === $node['id']
            ));
        }
        unset($node);

        return $topLevel;
    }
}

wiring.note: Built once per request in AuthMiddleware (already has the session and is already computing the auth_user Twig global) and exposed as the `menu` Twig global. Registered in app/dependencies.php as \App\Support\MenuBuilder::class => \DI\autowire(), and injected into AuthMiddleware's constructor wherever it is instantiated (routes/web.php).

menu_registry_pattern.sidebar_render_note: sidebar.twig loops `{% for item in menu %}`, rendering an <details> accordion when `item.children` is non-empty and a plain <a> otherwise. A small `{% set icons = {...} %}` dict at the top of sidebar.twig maps icon keys to inline SVG — that dict is the ONLY part of sidebar.twig a new module may need to touch (to add a new icon key), never the loop/render logic itself.

verified_gotchas.description: Bugs that only surfaced by actually running the generated app end-to-end (login, CSRF POST, session persistence across requests) — NOT visible from reading docs or vendor source alone. Added 2026-08-06 after the first full boilerplate run. Treat every one of these as MANDATORY, not optional advice — the app is broken without them.
verified_gotchas.twig_middleware_wiring: Slim\Views\TwigMiddleware::createFromContainer($app) resolves the Twig instance via the container but NEVER sets the 'view' request attribute (its internal $attributeName stays null) — Twig::fromRequest() then always throws RuntimeException. Use TwigMiddleware::create($app, $twigInstance, 'view') instead.
verified_gotchas.middleware_add_order_includes_twig: index_php_strict_rules.middleware_execution_order must also account for TwigMiddleware: add() order is [CsrfViewMiddleware, Guard, TwigMiddleware, RoutingMiddleware (addRoutingMiddleware), BodyParsingMiddleware (addBodyParsingMiddleware), ErrorMiddleware (addErrorMiddleware)] — actual execution order (Slim is FILO: first add() = LAST to execute) is the reverse: Error -> BodyParsing -> Routing -> Twig -> Guard -> CsrfView -> handler. TwigMiddleware MUST execute before CsrfViewMiddleware, which is why it is added AFTER Guard/CsrfView even though it runs earlier.
verified_gotchas.odan_session_get_has_no_default_param: Odan\Session\SessionInterface::get(string $key) takes exactly ONE parameter — there is no `get($key, $default)` overload like Laravel/Symfony. Calling it with a second argument does not error (PHP ignores extra args) but the 'default' is silently never applied; a missing key always returns null. Use `$session->get($key) ?? $default` instead.
verified_gotchas.session_never_persisted_without_save: Odan\Session\PhpSession keeps all set()/remove()/getFlash() mutations in an in-memory ArrayObject snapshot taken at start(). It ONLY writes that snapshot back to the real $_SESSION superglobal when save() is called explicitly (save() does `$_SESSION = (array) $this->storage; session_write_close();`). If save() is never called, login appears to succeed (302 redirect) but the very next request has an empty session. Call $session->save() in the innermost middleware, right after `$handler->handle($request)` returns.
verified_gotchas.csrf_storage_conflicts_with_session_save: Slim\Csrf\Guard's default storage writes CSRF token pairs DIRECTLY into $_SESSION['csrf'] by reference, bypassing Odan's ArrayObject entirely. Once CsrfViewMiddleware calls session->save() (see above), that save() OVERWRITES $_SESSION wholesale with Odan's stale pre-Guard snapshot, deleting the token Guard just issued — every POST fails CSRF validation on the very next request. Fix: pass Guard a custom ArrayAccess+Countable+Iterator storage object that reads/writes through SessionInterface::get()/set() (see App\Support\SessionCsrfStorage in the starter boilerplate) so CSRF tokens live in the SAME tracked storage as everything else.
verified_gotchas.rakit_validation_has_no_string_rule: Rakit\Validation ships no 'string' rule at all (confirmed against vendor/rakit/validation/src/Rules — Required, Max, Min, Email, etc. exist, 'string' does not). 'required|string|max:255' throws RuleNotFoundException at runtime. Just omit it: 'required|max:255'. Only add a type rule (array/integer/numeric/boolean) when the field really is that type.
verified_gotchas.eloquent_pagination_needs_separate_packa: Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder::paginate() throws 'Class "Illuminate\Pagination\Paginator" not found' unless illuminate/pagination is required separately in composer.json — it is NOT pulled in by illuminate/database. Add it explicitly whenever a CRUD list view uses ->paginate().
verified_gotchas.no_larastan_for_standalone_eloquent: larastan/larastan (needed to make PHPStan understand Eloquent's magic __callStatic/__get) hard-crashes with 'Undefined constant Larastan\Larastan\LARAVEL_VERSION' because it requires a full illuminate/foundation Laravel Application, which this project intentionally does not have. Do NOT add larastan. Instead add targeted `ignoreErrors` regex patterns to phpstan.neon for 'Call to an undefined static method App\\Models\\...' and 'Access to an undefined property App\\Models\\...' — these are correct at runtime, PHPStan just can't see Eloquent's magic without Larastan.

execution_pipeline.description: 10-Step Mandatory File Generation Contract for every feature/CRUD request

steps.name: form_requests
requirements: NO_STRING_RULE: Rakit\Validation has NO 'string' rule (verified against vendor/rakit/validation/src/Rules — confirmed missing by actually running the app, see project_brain_protocol.known_issues_log pattern). NEVER write 'required|string|max:255'. A plain text field only needs 'required|max:255'; only add a type rule (array/integer/numeric/boolean) when the field really is that type.
steps.template:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
namespace App\Requests;

use Rakit\Validation\Validator;
use Exception;

class {Action}{ModelName}Request
{
    public static function validate(array $data): array
    {
        $validator = new Validator;
        $validation = $validator->make($data, [
            'nama' => 'required|max:255',
        ]);
        $validation->validate();
        if ($validation->fails()) {
            throw new Exception($validation->errors()->firstOfAll()[0]);
        }
        return $validation->getValidData();
    }
}

steps.name: service_layer
requirements: ALSO_ENSURE_EXISTS (do not overwrite if present): app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php — see canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern.hooks_class_template and hook_protocol

steps.name: view_templates
steps.template_instructions: Always include `<input type="hidden" name="{{ csrf.keys.name }}" value="{{ csrf.name }}">` and `<input type="hidden" name="{{ csrf.keys.value }}" value="{{ csrf.value }}">` in all POST forms. Delete actions MUST use the `js-confirm-delete` form class (handled by public/assets/vendor/js/app.js via SweetAlert2) instead of native `onsubmit="confirm(...)"`. base.twig MUST also render `<meta name="csrf-name" content="{{ csrf.name }}">` and `<meta name="csrf-value" content="{{ csrf.value }}">` in <head>, plus a `<div id="app-loader" class="hidden fixed inset-0 z-50 ...">` element — both are read by app.js for the Axios CSRF header and the global loading overlay.

steps.name: sidebar_navigation
requirements: APPEND_ONE_ENTRY_ONLY (see canonical_snippets.menu_registry_pattern.menu_php_template): id, label, route, icon, permission, parent

NEVER_HAND_EDIT_SIDEBAR_TWIG: resources/views/partials/sidebar.twig is a generic renderer over app/menu.php and must never be edited to add a nav link — if it needs a NEW icon key, add it to the `icons` map at the top of sidebar.twig, nothing else in that file changes

permission_filtering_is_automatic: App\Support\MenuBuilder already filters by session permissions; do not wrap menu.php entries in {% if can(...) %} — that was the OLD per-module hand-edit pattern, now obsolete

owasp_top_ten_compliance.A01_Broken_Access_Control: Enforce RBAC middleware + Data Scope validation in Service layer. Deny access by default.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A02_Cryptographic_Failures: Use password_hash(PASSWORD_BCRYPT) and bin2hex(random_bytes(32)). Mask sensitive log data.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A03_Injection: 100% Parameterized queries via Eloquent ORM. Twig auto-escaping. Ban exec() and system().
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A04_Insecure_Design: Strict 5-Layer isolation, DB::transaction auto-rollback, anti double-submit loaders.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A05_Security_Misconfiguration: Zero hardcoded credentials (.env only). Mask stack traces in production. HttpOnly/Secure cookies.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A06_Vulnerable_Components: Strict NO-CDN Policy. Serve all JS/CSS/Fonts locally from /assets/vendor/. HALT AND FATAL ERROR IF AI PUTS <link href="https://cdn..."> OR <script src="https://..."> IN TWIG FILES.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A07_Authentication_Failures: Call $session->regenerateId() via Odan\Session\SessionInterface on login. Generic auth errors ('Email/password salah'). DO NOT use raw $_SESSION.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A08_Integrity_Failures: Mandatory CSRF validation on mutating HTTP methods (provided globally by slim/csrf). Validate file upload MIME and rename files.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A09_Logging_Failures: Mandatory AuditService calls for CUD operations and security events to var/log/app.log.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A10_SSRF: Strictly whitelist external HTTP domains if making outbound API calls.

database_transactions.pattern: Wrap multi-table CUD operations in DB::transaction(function() { ... }) for automatic rollback on failure.

centralized_error_handling.pattern: Catch exceptions centrally. Show full trace in APP_ENV=local, hide DB trace and log secretly in APP_ENV=production.

rate_limiting_and_session_expiry.pattern: Throttle login endpoints to max 5 failed attempts/15 mins per IP. Destroy session after 30 mins idle.

env_boot_validation.pattern: Verify required .env keys (APP_KEY, DB_HOST, DB_DATABASE) on application startup.

static_analysis.pattern: Code must pass PHPStan Level 5 analysis with 0 errors before deployment.

automated_testing.pattern: Generate feature/unit test in tests/Feature/{ModelName}Test.php for every new Service created.

project_brain_protocol.on_init: AI must inspect project directory and auto-generate PROJECT_BRAIN.json using the exact schema in 'schema_example' below. NEVER invent a different structure — a small model that reinvents the schema each session breaks continuity.
project_brain_protocol.on_task_complete: AI MUST update 'current_state' (last_feature, last_migration) and 'known_issues_log' in PROJECT_BRAIN.json.
